descriptors.definition: The Central Government provides financial grants to the Board through parliamentary appropriation, which forms part of the established SEBI General Fund. The Comptroller and Auditor-General of India conducts the audit of the Board accounts and submits certified statements and reports to the Central Government.
inclusion: Central Government grants
SEBI General Fund constitution and application
Preparation and CAG audit of annual accounts
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from penalties and adjudication provisions under subsequent sections by focusing exclusively on internal fund constitution, grants, and CAG financial auditing.

descriptors.definition: Persons registered as intermediaries or listed companies face monetary penalties for specific defaults such as failing to enter into client agreements, provide required returns, or redress investor grievances. These statutory penalties carry daily fines subject to an overall ceiling amount.
inclusion: Penalty for failure to furnish information or returns
Penalty for failure to enter into agreements with clients
Penalty for failure to redress investor grievances
exclusion: Board general funding and audit procedures
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general administrative directions by imposing specific, quantifiable monetary penalties for statutory defaults by intermediaries and companies.

descriptors.concept_name: Establishment, Jurisdiction, Authority And Procedure Of Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT)
descriptors.definition: The Central Government establishes the Securities Appellate Tribunal by notification to exercise statutory adjudicatory powers and jurisdiction. The Tribunal consists of a Presiding Officer, Judicial Members, and Technical Members sitting in benches that include at least one judicial and one technical member.
inclusion: Establishment and notification of SAT
Tribunal composition and bench constitution
Qualifications for Presiding Officer and members
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from SEBI adjudicating officers by constituting an independent appellate tribunal with multi-member benches for hearing appeals against regulatory orders.

descriptors.definition: The Securities Appellate Tribunal functions through designated benches comprising judicial and technical members appointed based on statutory judicial background criteria. These benches operate primarily from Mumbai or notified alternative locations under the administrative direction of the Presiding Officer.
inclusion: Bench jurisdiction and sitting arrangements
Member transfer protocols
Statutory qualification thresholds for judicial and technical appointments
nearby_distinctions: Focuses on the structural composition, bench formation, and qualification criteria of SAT members rather than general penal provisions.

descriptors.definition: The Central Government holds statutory authority to issue written policy directions to the Board and can supersede the Board for a limited period under circumstances of grave emergency, persistent default, or public interest. Upon supersession, all members vacate their offices and Board properties temporarily vest in the Central Government.
inclusion: Central Government power to issue policy directions
Grounds and effects of superseding the Board
Reconstitution of the Board after supersession
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard regulatory oversight by addressing extreme structural interventions such as government supersession and binding policy directives.

descriptors.concept_name: SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 Scope
descriptors.definition: The SEBI Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements Regulations consolidate listing conditions and align listing agreement clauses with the Companies Act. These rules apply to entities accessing stock exchanges to list designated securities such as specified equity shares, debt securities, depository receipts, and mutual fund units.
instrument_references: SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015
inclusion: Consolidation of existing listing agreements
Applicability criteria across various capital market segments
Scope covering equities, debt, and mutual fund units
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from the SEBI Act provisions by providing a unified regulatory framework specifically governing post-listing obligations and periodic disclosures of issuers.

descriptors.concept_name: Scope and Applicability of Listing Regulations
descriptors.definition: The Listing Regulations establish unified periodic disclosure standards and corporate governance principles for entities with designated securities listed on recognized stock exchanges. Once provisions become applicable based on market capitalization or debt thresholds, they continue to apply even if the entity subsequently falls below those thresholds.
instrument_references: SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015
inclusion: Applicability to specified securities, debt, and depository receipts
Continuation of applicability despite falling below thresholds
Broad principles for periodic disclosures and corporate governance
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from initial public offering guidelines by focusing strictly on continuing obligations and governance after securities are listed on a stock exchange.

descriptors.concept_name: Introduction and Structure of Listing Regulations
descriptors.definition: SEBI issued the Listing Regulations to streamline capital market listing norms into a single comprehensive document containing both substantive provisions and procedural schedules. These regulations enforce continuous disclosure norms and corporate governance principles across diverse market segments.
instrument_references: SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015
inclusion: Structure dividing regulations into substantive main body and procedural schedules
Effective implementation date and harmonization goals
exclusion: Internal statutory funding of the regulatory board
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from the SEBI Act by providing the operational architecture of listing rules divided between main regulations and schedules.

descriptors.concept_name: Board of Directors Composition under Listing Regulations
descriptors.definition: The board of directors of a listed entity must maintain an optimum combination of executive and non-executive directors, including at least one woman director and a specified minimum percentage of non-executive members. Top listed entities determined by market capitalization must also appoint independent directors pursuant to specific governance mandates.
inclusion: Optimum combination of executive and non-executive directors
Mandatory inclusion of at least one woman director
Independent director mandates for top listed entities
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general disclosure obligations by establishing direct structural mandates for board composition and governance leadership.

descriptors.concept_name: Common Obligations of Listed Entities and Compliance Officers
descriptors.definition: Listed entities must ensure that key managerial personnel, directors, and promoters fulfill their regulatory responsibilities, including the appointment of a qualified company secretary as compliance officer. The compliance officer oversees regulatory conformity, reporting coordination, information filing accuracy, and grievance redressal monitoring.
inclusion: General compliance obligations of KMPs and promoters
Mandatory appointment of qualified company secretary as compliance officer
Share transfer agent appointment or in-house facility management
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from periodic disclosure filings by establishing internal administrative personnel requirements and general compliance duties for corporate officers.

descriptors.definition: Listed entities must file specified reports and statements with recognized stock exchanges on a quarterly basis, including grievance redressal statistics, corporate governance reports, and shareholding patterns. Additional quarterly disclosures cover statement of deviation in fund utilization and standalone financial results within stipulated timeframes.
inclusion: Quarterly investor complaints and grievance statements
Corporate governance compliance reports
Shareholding pattern statements and capital restructuring disclosures
Statement of deviation in issue proceeds utilization
Standalone financial results submission timelines
exclusion: Initial public offer draft prospectus drafting
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from continuous event-based disclosures by enforcing regular periodic reporting cycles within strict calendar deadlines following each quarter.
